headline_marked: 6 million [[CVs of Bangladeshis for sale]] on Dark Web
headline: 6 million CVs of Bangladeshis for sale on Dark Web
summary: A hacker group claims to have stolen data from BDJobs, though the platform denies any breach of its own systems.
details: A hacker group calling themselves 'Madarx' has advertised the sale of 6 million CVs of Bangladeshi citizens on the website 'DarkForums.ru'.
The hackers claim the data was sourced from the BDJobs database, including names, phone numbers, addresses, emails, educational qualifications, and professional experience.
A copy of the database is being offered for $1,000, with the hackers stating they will sell the information to a maximum of five buyers via payment methods like Paytm, Wise, PayU, and Binance.
To support their claim, the group released 148 sample CVs. Analysis shows most of these are old, with many last updated between 2011 and 2017.
BDJobs founder and CEO Fahim Mashrur has denied the breach, stating the platform prioritizes user security and has controls over who can view profiles.
Mashrur noted that while hundreds of thousands of registered employers can view candidate data for recruitment, any employer selling this data to third parties would face legal action.
Cyber security expert Tanvir Hassan Zoha warned that such data allows criminals to create full digital profiles for targeted phishing, fake job offers, identity theft, and financial fraud.

headline_marked: 10,000kg of fertilizer [[taken by angry farmers]] in Kurigram
headline: 10,000kg of fertilizer taken by angry farmers in Kurigram
summary: Farmers broke into a dealer's warehouse in Bhurungamari, Kurigram, after allegations of delays in distribution.
details: Angry farmers broke into a fertilizer dealer's warehouse in the Shilkuri union of Bhurungamari, Kurigram, and took away approximately 10,000 kg of urea fertilizer.
The incident occurred around 11:00 AM on Sunday, August 23, at the M/S Shah Amanat Dealer Point. Over 200 farmers gathered at the point, but the warehouse remained closed, leading to the frustration.

The dealer, Taifur Rahman Mukul, had been allocated 1,320 sacks of urea fertilizer, with 340 sacks currently in stock. Farmers alleged that the dealer delayed distribution despite having sufficient stock.
The crowd broke the warehouse door and took 197 sacks (9,850 kg) of urea fertilizer. Police arrived at the scene shortly after to prevent further looting and protect the remaining stock.
Bhurungamari Police Station OC Azimuddin stated that while the demand in the union was 4,000 sacks, the total allocation was only 1,320 sacks, causing fear among farmers regarding availability.
Upazila Agriculture Officer Abdul Jabbar clarified that there is no shortage of urea fertilizer in the upazila, as the required 680 metric tons for August were received and are being distributed.

Bhurungamari Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Amrit Debnath confirmed that peaceful distribution was happening elsewhere in the union, but some 'disorderly people' looted the fertilizer. He added that police have recovered 33 sacks from 33 farmers so far.
Law enforcement agencies are continuing efforts to recover the remaining sacks of fertilizer.
